comment: 🔴 65.2 — the high-water mark for rendered prose, in WORDS A PERSON HAS TO READ, per portal. `npm run prose` FAILS when one rises. Lowering it is the work; raising it is a decision somebody makes on purpose, in a diff, with a reason in PLAN.md. A wall split into four keys is the same wall, which is why the unit is a word rather than a key. `origin` is where sprint 65 started and NOTHING writes to it: the accept line asks for half off every portal and 80% off the public site, and a baseline that follows the work downward cannot answer that. The first numbers here attributed `home.*` to the public site and `radar.*` to it as well; both were corrected by grepping the call sites, which moved 221 words into the patient app and 201 into shared. The public figure fell from 5836 to 5460 for that reason alone, and no prose was removed by it. A second correction moved `pted.*` and `pracc.*` (220 words) from the patient app to the clinician's: both render on `app/(app)/patients/[id]/page.tsx`, and they are named for what they are ABOUT rather than who reads them. A third correction moved `cassess.*` (71 words) to the clinician's: it renders in `components/assessments/clinician-assessments.tsx`. A fourth moved `room.*` and `preset.*` (455 words) to the patient app: `room.*` renders only in the join flow, the patient room, the rating form and the booking sheet, and `preset` is the patient's password reset. 🔴 AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT WHAT A READER MEETS. It swept the dictionary and the CMS and could not see a sentence typed straight into a component, of which `components/pay/pay-flow.tsx` alone had fourteen. Worse, it put the two gates in 65.24's pass in opposition: keying a literal is the work `verify:sprint37l` asks for, and under a dictionary-only sweep it RAISED the portal's number. The sweep now counts markup literals too, through the same `literalsIn` the i18n ratchet uses, so moving a sentence between the two is neutral here and an improvement there. `origin` was re-measured on the commit before sprint 65 with the corrected instrument, in a worktree, so every percentage on this file compares like with like: admin 2564, clinic 1485, clinician 7625, partner 1410, patient 4719, public 5460, shared 1319, sponsor 1193. The admin figure is what it is because the admin console is English by decision (37L.3) and its markup is now counted; it did not grow. 🔴 `legal` IS ITS OWN NUMBER FROM SPRINT 65 ON. 65.14 asks for 80% off every page of the public site and was written about the marketing pages; a privacy notice, the terms, the HIPAA page and the security page are not walls of text, they are the product, and cutting one by 80% removes disclosures a regulator expects a reader to have been given, which is 65.23's failure in its most expensive form. Their 1377 words moved out of `public` and into `legal`, whose number may not rise either, so a marketing paragraph pushed into `terms` shows up rather than vanishing. 🔴 ONE MORE THING THE PUBLIC NUMBER UNDERSTATES. `app/(public)/` is exempt from `scanI18n`, on the ground that it renders CMS rows published in both languages — true of `[slug]`, false of the hand-built `for-clinics` and `integrations` pages, whose text was typed into the markup and was therefore invisible to BOTH gates. Sprint 65 moved `for-clinics` into the dictionary at a third of its length, which makes roughly 250 words newly COUNTED here while being fewer words on the screen. The ratchet's figure is the conservative one.

translated.comment: 🔴 65.3 — EVERY REMOVED BLOCK, AND WHAT NOW CARRIES THE RULE IT HELD. 'Nothing is deleted, everything is translated': a shorter screen that dropped a disclaimer is a regression, not an improvement. This lived in comments beside each replacement until C205's rule pointed out the obvious: a record only a comment holds is a record no check can read. It is data now, so `verify:sprint65` can assert that every key named here is genuinely gone from both dictionaries and that the component named beside it genuinely exists.

c349: 🔴 admin ENDED WHERE IT STARTED, 2564, and the route there is the point. C349 added six words to `/admin/vault`: column headings on a month table that replaced two bars whose figures were reachable only by hovering a `title=` attribute, which shows nothing on a touchscreen and reaches a screen reader as an afterthought. C351 added twelve more, warning an operator that the rejection they are about to give is the one that deletes somebody's identity documents. 🔴 THE FIRST INSTINCT WAS TO RECORD THE RISE AND ARGUE FOR IT, AND 65.2 REFUSED, which is the gate being better than the person operating it: `comment` says a rise is a decision somebody makes on purpose, and `verify:sprint65` says a baseline may never exceed its origin, and the second is the one that binds. So the sprint paid for its own words, five times, and every cut is a real duplication rather than a shave. The sentence 'a wrong number looks like help, presses like help and does nothing' was on `/admin/settings` TWICE, once in the red card and once beside the field an operator types the number into; the card's copy went and the one they read while typing stayed. The crisis block's 'leave both blank until somebody has checked it' restated its own first sentence. `/admin/numbers` carried the lock rule AND the argument for it, and the argument moved into the source, where the next person to shorten LOCK_DAYS will read it. `/admin/vault`'s subtitle described, column by column, the table that now sits below it. And the chart's legend was a second list of the three names the table already prints, so the colour swatches moved into the column headings and the legend went. 🔴 That last one is the sprint 65 move in miniature: the legend was words explaining a picture, and putting the picture next to the word it labels removed the need for both.
sprint73: 🔴 shared 1147→1226 is a RISE of 79 and admin 2479→2476 is a fall, and the two numbers together are the sprint. Sprint 73 built the Egyptian payment rail, because `topUpPot` refuses an Egyptian entity and the consequence nobody had costed was that the ENTIRE Egyptian market had no way to pay us. The rise is the payer's screen: `components/billing/pay-by-transfer.tsx`, which shows the account details, takes the reference, and holds the waiting state a person can close their phone on. 🔴 IT WAS WRITTEN IN ENGLISH FIRST AND THAT WAS THE FINDING. A hundred words of English on the screen where an Egyptian patient hands over money, caught by `verify:sprint37l` against a patient floor of ZERO, which is the surface that floor exists to protect. So it is keyed in both languages rather than counted as debt, the patient surface stays at 0 and the shared literal count is unchanged at 72 — the words moved into the dictionary, which is where the two ratchets agree an improvement looks like this. 🔴 AND THE COPY WAS CUT BEFORE THE FLOOR WAS RAISED: six strings shortened in both languages, roughly halving them, and the raise is to 1226 against an ORIGIN of 1319, so it is still 7% below where sprint 65 started. `verify:sprint65` would have refused anything above 1319 and did not need to. The admin half was paid in full the usual way: the queue screen cost 52 words and five more walls were shortened across the partner manager, the therapist panel, settings and the settings editor.
sprint73b: 🔴 shared 1226→1241 is a RISE of 15 and admin held level at 2476 while gaining a whole settings form, and the fifteen are the sentence a finance team actually needed. The sponsor's coverage control used to say '10%' and nothing else. It now says: at 10% you pay $2 of a $20 session, so your balance of $200 covers about 100 sessions. That is the sum they would do on paper before agreeing to anything, and a percentage without it is a number nobody can make a decision from. 🔴 IT IS ALSO THE ONLY WAY THE SLIDER MEANS ANYTHING: sprint 73 locked the control behind Edit and Save precisely so somebody reads that line between the two acts. The average session price it rests on is a SETTING, `sponsor.averageSessionCents`, not a constant on the screen, because a projection built on an average nobody can change is a projection nobody can correct. The admin half was paid in full as usual: the transfer-fields editor cost 51 words and nine walls were shortened across settings, the ledger adjuster, taxonomy, the dashboard, the audit log, radar and announcements.
sprint73c: 🔴 shared 1241→1284, and it is the Egyptian company's payment screen. `TransferTopUp` is the form a finance team fills in after sending us money: the account details, how much, the reference. It exists because `topUpPot` refuses their entity, so without it the three call centres this whole go-to-market is built on cannot pay us at all. The copy was cut before the floor moved — the waiting message, the instruction, the unconfigured notice and a placeholder, roughly halved — and 1284 is still 3% below the ORIGIN of 1319, so `verify:sprint65` did not need to refuse anything. 🔴 THE PATIENT'S EQUIVALENT COST NOTHING, because sprint 73 keyed it in both languages instead. That is the line this file now holds in two places: a screen a customer pays on is translated, and English on it is a defect rather than a decision. A sponsor's finance team is the one payer surface where English is the working language in this market, and that judgement is written in `_i18n-coverage.json` so the next person can disagree with it.

raised.comment: 🔴 NOT RAISED IN THE END, AND THE ATTEMPT IS THE RECORD. Sprint 75 added two admin controls the product could not operate without, both of them forms, which is the most expensive prose there is. The first move was to raise the admin mark from 2548 to 2606 under this file's own rule that raising it is a decision made on purpose in a diff. `verify:sprint65` refused it: a baseline may never sit above its ORIGIN, and admin's origin is 2564. So the form was PAID FOR instead, by tightening nine strings that were carrying their rules in more words than the rules needed. Admin finished at 2562, two words under origin and fourteen under where it started, with two controls on the screen that were not there before. That is the ratchet working exactly as designed: it did not stop the feature, it made the feature earn its room.

addedBy.the back office team form: `staff` and `manager` have been roles since sprint 20, five admin pages sit behind requireStaff() and the board behind requireManager(), and NOTHING in the product could create an account with either. The plan pays two support staff from month one to work a payments queue they had no way to reach, so the only way to work it was to share the owner's login, which ends the audit trail.
addedBy.the welcome credit field: The plan promises every company $100 of pot credit, and both ways money reaches a pot enforce a $5,000 minimum, so the one commercial offer the go-to-market rests on was unreachable by any screen.

raised.paidFor: apartner.neverMints, apartner.body, acheckin.rateBody, acheckin.noBodies, acheckin.body, aclinic.body, asponsor.body, asponsor.drift, tver.underReviewBody, tver.savedListNote, and the copilot allowance hint in components/admin/settings-editor.tsx. Every rule each of them carried is still on the screen; only the words are fewer.

sprint75vat: 🔴 PATIENT 3846 -> 3873, RAISED ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS THE ONLY RAISE IN THIS SPRINT. `app/(patient)/error.tsx` did not exist: a patient whose page threw got the framework's own blank boundary, in English, with the SOS orb gone. The replacement keeps the orb and says three things, and each one is load-bearing at the worst moment somebody has on this product: nothing you did caused it, nothing you sent is lost, and the crisis button still works. Twenty-seven words after trimming, against an origin of 4719. It was NOT paid for out of the patient app because there was nothing left to pay with: `npm run prose --portal patient` reports ZERO blocks of 25 words or more. The prefix was also unattributed until now, sitting in `other` where no ratchet counted it, which is the hole this entry closes as much as the words. 🔴 SHARED 1284 -> 1239 AND CLINICIAN 6285 -> 6282 ARE FALLS, not raises: `transfer.taxNote` added four words to tell an Egyptian payer why 1,140 pounds is the figure for a 1,000 pound session, and the partner usage meter paid for them five times over by dropping a sentence that repeated the banner above it.
sprint76: 🔴 SPONSOR 996 -> 1031, for the top-up stepper, and the prefix was misattributed before it was counted. `topup.*` renders in `components/billing/top-up-stepper.tsx` and nowhere else, which is `/sponsor/pot`; the letter rule had it under the CLINICIAN on the `t`, so the first run of this sprint reported a therapist's portal growing by 35 words it does not contain. That is the same misattribution the note above the portal map was written about, and it is the second time the `t` has caused it. The 35 words buy a screen that replaced a free text box in dollars: on a rail with no processor, a typed amount is how somebody sends $5 or $50,000 by slipping on a zero, and neither is reversible. Origin is 1193 and this sits 14% under it.
sprint76b: 🔴 SHARED 1239 -> 1270 and CLINICIAN 6282 -> 6304, both bought deliberately. SHARED is the payment popup and the pending bar: `pop.*` and `bar.*` render for a patient, a clinician, a clinic manager and a company finance team, so they belong beside `transfer` rather than under whichever portal the letter rule guessed. They were unattributed on the first run and showed up as an `other` bucket with no ratchet, which is a hole in the map rather than a cost. CLINICIAN is `tnew.patientPays` and `tnew.weHold`: an Egyptian clinician setting a price can now be told what their PATIENT will actually be asked for, tax included, because on the transfer rail the country is known before the price is typed. The old line said only that the patient 'also pays VAT, set by their country', which is the honest sentence on the card rail and a needlessly vague one here. Both sit well under origin.
sprint76c: 🔴 THE SCANNER'S BLIND SPOT, AND WHAT IT COST TO CLOSE HONESTLY. Wrapping every dollar figure in <Money> moved the formatter off its line, and the prose sweep skips a line that calls one inline. So prose that had sat in the product for sprints became VISIBLE all at once: admin jumped 2562 -> 2597, six words ABOVE its origin of 2564, which `verify:sprint65` refuses. None of it was written this sprint. The honest answer was not to raise a mark past its origin but to PAY, so four genuine admin walls were shortened: the held-balances incident notice now names `journal` instead of describing it, the netting toggle drops a sentence about what is forbidden, and two dictionary strings lost a clause each. Admin finished at 2546, eighteen words BELOW origin and sixteen below where the sprint started. Patient 3873 -> 3875 and shared 1270 -> 1272 are four words for the same reason, both far under origin, and patient's own exposure was paid rather than recorded: 'in credit' became pbill.inCredit in both dictionaries the moment the scanner could see it.
sprint76d: 🔴 SHARED 1272 -> 1280: eight words, four payer-type labels in two languages. The one payment sheet now names which payer it is for at the top, because four payers meet identical bank details underneath and a clinic manager could not tell at a glance whether the sheet was the practice's bill or an employer's pot. It is also the first thing a payments operator needs when somebody sends a screenshot of this screen asking why the amount is wrong. Still 3% under origin.
sprint76e: 🔴 ADMIN 2546 -> 2563 for two screens that did not exist, and the 17 words were MEASURED rather than estimated. The transfers queue links every payer's name to their page and two of the three payers had nowhere to go, so a company profile and a patient payments page were written. Estimating their cost by eye was wrong twice, because this sweep counts a repeated string ONCE: cutting three 'Not given' placeholders saved two words and not six. The honest way to price a change is to remove it and re-measure, which is what settled it at 21 words, trimmed to 17 by dropping a sentence the amber heading above it already said. Admin ends one word under origin.
sprint76i: 🔴 CLINICIAN 6297 -> 6368 for a control that did not exist, and SHARED 1305 -> 1280 which is a fall. A clinician ran an offline session with two people on one microphone, every line of the transcript read `Speaker`, and there was no way anywhere to correct a single one. The diariser is called before the note and it did read those lines: it declined to guess, because the recording is cut on a clock rather than at the turns, so most chunks on one microphone hold the end of one turn and the start of the next, and C35's rule is that a half-correct label is worse than none in a clinical record. `unknown` was the honest answer. What was missing was anyone saying so, and any remedy. So: the session page's transcript now shows who said each line and offers you / them / not sure on every one that no separated voice owns, a clinician's own correction clears the `worked out from the words` marker because it is the one attribution with a person behind it, and when most of a transcript is unattributed the screen explains why in three sentences rather than showing forty lines that read as broken software. Seventy one words for the whole feature, trimmed twice: the blurb went from fourteen words to five once the buttons made it obvious, and the explanation lost a clause. Sixteen percent under origin. SHARED fell because nothing was added to it and the payment sheet lost its in-sheet cancel copy when that control moved to the payment entry.
sprint76h: 🔴 PATIENT 3878 -> 3885 AND PUBLIC 2836 -> 2870, and only the first is prose this sprint wrote. PATIENT is eight words for three keys: Minimise, Back to your session, Still on. They are the whole vocabulary of a control that lets somebody take a phone call in the middle of a therapy session without dropping out of it, and people who drop out of a therapy session in the middle do not come back. It was NOT paid for out of the patient app because there is nothing left to pay with: `npm run prose --portal patient` reports ZERO blocks of 25 words or more, and has since sprint 75 recorded the same thing. Eighteen percent under origin. PUBLIC is 34 words that were already in the product and were counted by nobody. `hdemo.*` is the chrome around the demo session in the marketing hero and renders only in `components/public/blocks.tsx`; the letter rule had no entry for `h`, so it arrived as an `unattributed` bucket with no ratchet on it at all. That is a hole in the map rather than a cost, the same one `home` fell into from the other direction, and closing it is why the number moved. Thirty percent under origin.
sprint76g: 🔴 CLINICIAN 6304 -> 6297, and the whole therapist payment side was rebuilt inside it. The plans are pricing cards now, with the one they are on marked, and choosing another shows four sentences about what it costs, what it does to the per-session fee, how cancelling works and which rail takes the money, before any money moves. That is genuinely new prose and it was paid for twice over. Twenty-eight dead `tplan.*` keys came out: they are the credit-ladder era, two repricings ago, referenced by nothing, and still counted by this sweep because it counts the dictionary rather than the render. Then the card header stopped repeating the prices the cards now carry beside themselves, and `tplan.plansBody` went with it for the same reason. What stays in the header is C209, which a comparison grid cannot carry: the AI fee is never charged when a patient declines to be recorded, so no amount rides on the most vulnerable person in the room saying yes. The credits slider is gone entirely, with its three keys. Net seven words under where the sprint found it, 17% under origin, for a screen that now says more.
sprint76f: 🔴 SHARED 1280 -> 1318, and 27 of the 38 are one sentence that decides whether money can be allocated at all. There is no processor on this rail: a transfer arrives in our bank as a line with somebody's name on it and nothing linking it to an account. A payer who sends the money and closes the page has paid us and cannot be credited, so the operator holds a bank line they cannot match and the payer holds a session that never unlocks. Pressing Submit is what makes the two halves findable, and it used to be implied by a button label reading 'I have paid' — which describes something they did in a banking app, not the thing the button does. It is stated now, in red, above the field it is about, and the button says Submit. The rest is the bar learning to tell an OPEN payment from a submitted one, which is the difference between waiting on them and waiting on us. Trimmed twice to land one word under origin.
sprint76j: 🔴 CLINICIAN 6368 -> 6484, and it buys a page that did not exist. The therapist's view of a patient was a chart: a name, four editable fields, two links and a list of sessions. It is a profile now, and every paragraph in the raise is a question somebody had no answer to. Whether this person has claimed their own record, which decides whether the face at the top is theirs and whether they can take your access away. What the invitation on it does before it spends their money: a video session at your rate, paid before they join, sent to the number already on the chart. Why the copilot underneath is the same conversation as the copilot page rather than a second one. And the sentence the walk-in line needed, because a chart with no phone on it now exists and reads as broken without one. Trimmed once by 44 words after the first measurement: four of the six new bodies said the same thing in half the length, and the two that carry a consequence (a price, a revocation) were left alone. Paid down in the same diff where it could be: the copilot page stopped printing '3 sessions on record' and 'corrections applied' as English literals in the markup, which is five words off the patient column and, more to the point, two lines that were English on the Arabic page for as long as that page has existed. 15% under origin.
sprint76k2: 🔴 SHARED 1280 -> 1285, and the five are the only words in this product that no customer will ever read. `components/simulation-banner.tsx` renders on the simulation deployment and returns null everywhere else: null in development, null in production, null on every other branch, because it is gated on VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF being the simulation branch. The words are 'Simulation. Everybody here is invented.' 🔴 THEY ARE NOT DECORATION. The run produces a deployment somebody signs into six months later and reads as a therapist, a patient and an operator, and it looks exactly like the product because it IS the product: same code, same screens, same money. Nothing else on the page can tell them the people are invented, and a screen full of invented clinical records that does not say so is a screen somebody eventually quotes. The sweep counts the markup rather than the render condition, which is correct and is why this is recorded rather than argued away.

admin.why: 🔴 Two rises, recorded separately because they bought different things and the second is the larger. The first 94 words are /admin/actuals from 76.53: a table of what the company earned and spent each month plus the editable payroll, against an origin of 2564 with ten words of headroom and zero blocks of 25 words or more to pay with. 🔴 THE FURTHER 140 ARE 76.56 AND 76.57, AND WHAT THEY BUY IS TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE NOT VISIBLE FROM ANY SCREEN. The first: that table's Cash column was the `cash` ledger account accumulated from zero, which is what TRADING did to the balance and not the balance, so a company that put fifty thousand in and spent thirty read as minus thirty thousand. Where we stand now carries four figures — ours to spend, in the bank, burning, runway — and the editors under it hold the capital and the video, bank, hosting and accountancy bills nothing in the product buys. Twenty-four words of labels, eleven of prose, and one heading each. The second: a transfer receipt was a link that opened a photograph in another tab with no reference, no amount and no buttons, so every approval on the Egyptian rail was taken from memory about evidence in a different window. The modal puts the picture, the reference, the amount and the two decisions in one frame. 🔴 FORTY WORDS WERE PAID BEFORE THIS WAS WRITTEN, and every one of them improved the form: the same 'typing 0 removes that month' sentence was under each of seven cost blocks and is now one line above them; 'what they said it covers' was on the queue row AND in the modal and is now only where the question gets asked; the rejection placeholder was a second copy of the label beside it; and three safety paragraphs lost their second half without losing their rule. 2838 down to 2798. 🔴 SAME ARGUMENT AS EVERY ADMIN RISE SINCE SPRINT 71, which is 37L.3's: this console is staffed by us, in English, by decision. 🔴 AND THE RULE THAT DOES NOT BEND HELD: patient is still 0. 🔴 A FURTHER 108 IN 76.79, and they are the block guide on /admin/content: one paragraph each for `competitors`, `vendors` and `walkthrough`. 18.6 is why they exist. A block type with no editable text of its own reads as a broken editor to somebody who does not know that `pricing` reads platform_settings and that `walkthrough`'s steps are fixed in code; the guide is the thing that stops an operator going looking for numbers that are deliberately absent. Same 37L.3 argument as every admin entry above: the console is staffed by us, in English, by decision. 🔴 AND THE DOOR TO THE UI REFERENCE WAS PAID FOR RATHER THAN RECORDED. verify:reachable reported /design as a page no principal could get to, and linking it from /admin/content cost sixteen admin words. Nine came straight back off the link's own copy and the rest off five hints in the competitor editor, none of which lost a ruling: 'exactly as they publish it, with its unit' says what 'with its unit, exactly as they publish it, never a figure worked out from one' said. Admin came back to 2905, ONE BELOW where it started this round, so the baseline moved down rather than up.

public.why: 🔴 public 2870 -> 5164 and admin 2798 -> 2906, and the public one is the largest rise ever recorded in this file, so here is the argument it exists to make somebody type. 🔴 WHAT THE 2294 BOUGHT. Two reference surfaces the founder asked for by name. The first is the comparison against SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Upheal, Mentalyc and Lyra Health: five rivals, six rows each, both columns on every row, and one row per rival where the honest answer is that they are better. That block is 736 words and it is rendered on TWO pages, the pricing page where somebody is deciding and the homepage under the prices where the founder's own order for that page puts it, so it counts twice. The second is the pricing page's own feature grid and the two flows on the patients page. 🔴 IT IS REFERENCE MATERIAL RATHER THAN PROSE, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT AND ALSO ITS WEAKNESS. 65.14 asks for 80% off the public site and it was written about marketing paragraphs: a page that describes the product at length instead of showing it. A table of thirty claims with both sides stated is the opposite of that, and the rows sit behind tabs so a reader meets six at a time rather than thirty. The sweep counts what is in the markup, not what is on the screen, and it is right to: a reader who compares against two rivals reads twelve rows, and the sweep cannot know how many they will open. So this is recorded as a rise rather than argued away as a measurement artefact. 🔴 IT WAS PAID DOWN BEFORE IT WAS RECORDED. The `ours` column ran twelve words a cell against `theirs` at seven, which is the table arguing where the other column states, and eighteen cells were rewritten: 285 words to 213, which is 144 off the public number once doubled. The tightening improved the table on its own merits and would have been worth doing with no ratchet. 🔴 THE ONE TO RE-OPEN LATER: whether the homepage needs all five rivals or a three-row teaser linking to the pricing page. A teaser is 1100 public words back. It is not done here because a second, shorter copy of the same table is two things to correct the day a rival reprices, which is C60's shape, and the sprint that cut the comparison to one const shared by both pages did it for exactly that reason. 🔴 ADMIN'S 108 ARE THE BLOCK GUIDE, one paragraph each for `competitors`, `vendors` and `walkthrough` on /admin/content. 18.6 is why they are there: a block type with no editable text of its own reads as a broken editor to somebody who does not know that `pricing` reads platform_settings and `walkthrough`'s steps are fixed in code. The guide is the thing that stops an operator going looking for numbers that are deliberately absent. 🔴 AND NO OTHER PORTAL MOVED. shared went back to 1285 because three literals that landed on it were keyed rather than recorded; patient, clinician, clinic, sponsor, partner and legal are all level. 🔴 SPRINT 77 ADDED 194 MORE, recorded separately under `sprint77`: the five dead phone mockups became one working app and the three clinical demos got the controls their claims describe. 65 words were rewritten shorter before the rise was written down.

sprint77: 🔴 public 5164 -> 5358, and every other portal is level. 194 words, and 155 of them are two dictionaries that did not exist: `pat` (the patient app demo) and `dclin` (the three clinical demos). 🔴 WHAT THEY BOUGHT, AND IT IS A DELETION RATHER THAN AN ADDITION. Before this sprint the public site carried five separate phone mockups — sessions, steps, the radar, the journal, the summary — each one screen under a drawn bottom bar with five tabs that did nothing. A reader could see the app HAD a Sessions tab and had no way to find out what was on it, so the five pictures together described less of the product than one working phone does. They are now one component opened on five different tabs, the bar is live, and the radar books a session end to end. The five mockups became one app, and the words are the words that app says on its own screens: a price, a tax line, a total, and the sentence about no account placed at the step where somebody braces for a signup wall. 🔴 `dclin` IS 45 WORDS AND IT IS THREE CONTROLS. The transcript claims it runs live and now stops when a patient asks; the note claims it is a draft until approved and now has the approval on it; the risk banner claims it is a prompt rather than a safety net and now dismisses. Each of those three sentences was already on the page, unaccompanied by the thing it describes. 🔴 IT WAS PAID DOWN BEFORE IT WAS RECORDED. Eight strings were rewritten shorter in both languages — the homepage's new patient hero from 46 words to 24, `pat.bookedBody` 19 to 9, `pat.noAccount` 18 to 13, `pat.freeNow` 13 to 9, `pat.billingNote` 17 to 11, `dclin.dismissedBody` 24 to 13, `dclin.draftUntil` 10 to 5 — 65 words off before the number was written down, and the patients page's own hero body is shorter than it was. 🔴 AND 110 OF THE 194 ARE A REATTRIBUTION, NOT A PURCHASE. `pat` falls to `patient` under the letter rule, and it is the demo of the patient app rather than the app: a hero read by somebody deciding whether to use this, not by a person in distress. Charging it to the patient portal would be the misattribution the map's own header warns about, pointed the other way. The move is in `prose-sweep.ts` with the grep that proves where the prefix is used. 🔴 THE ONE TO RE-OPEN LATER: the radar hero's body is 64 words and is the largest single public block outside the comparison table. It was left alone here because its last sentence is an honesty claim `verify:claims` reads, and cutting it in the same pass as a ratchet rise is how a claim goes missing.
